title: Entry eval: latency vs cost scan (batching, cache, max_tokens)
content:
Purpose:
Quick scan to understand how batching, prefix/KV caching, and max_tokens caps interact with latency (p50/p95/p99), throughput, and per-request cost when onboarding new encoder-decoder and decoder-only variants. This is a working notebook for decisions on default serving presets for new models.

High-level hypothesis and motivation:
- Hypothesis: For short-turn prompts (<= 64 tokens) aggressive batching improves throughput and lowers cost but causes p95 tail inflation under microburst arrivals; prefix cache reduces per-token work but can introduce cache fragmentation when prompt diversity is high.
- We want a small decision tree for default recommendations: when to enable batching strong, when to pin cache, and sensible max_tokens defaults to bound tail cost.

Experimental scope and constraints:
- Models tested: small-open-decoder-v1 (3B-ish), mid-open-encoder-decoder-v1 (7B-ish), and a quantized 4-bit variant of the decoder model.
- Hardware: single A100-80GB host (dedicated test node) and one multi-tenant G4 cluster node for comparison.
- Arrival patterns: steady (poisson lambda 50 r/s), microburst (bursts of 200 r/s for 200ms every 10s using APIGW trace sample), and heavy-diverse (high prompt vocabulary to stress cache).
- Prompt sets: 3 curated prompt families — short-turn Q/A (avg 28 tokens), multi-sentence summarization (avg 180 tokens), and slot-filling templates (avg 72 tokens). Prompt set ~600 samples total.
- Sweep variables: batch_size_target (1, 8, 32, 64), max_tokens cap (64, 128, 256, 512), cache_mode (off, prefix-only, prefix+kv), quantization (fp16, int8/4bit).
- Metrics captured: per-request latency (p50/p95/p99), tokens/sec, GPU utilization, cost estimate (tokens * unit-model-cost + GPU-time amortized), request-eviction / cache-hit rate, and quality (ROUGE / exact-match proxies for small prompts).

Key results (summary):
- Short-turn family: best cost per request at batch_target 32 with prefix+kv cache enabled and max_tokens=64. Observed 4.2x reduction in per-request GPU time vs batch=1 without cache. BUT p95 increased by 45ms in microburst pattern (from 140ms to 185ms) due to queueing.
- Multi-sentence family: batching benefits saturated at batch_target 8 — larger batches increase overall latency for long sequences because batching groups longer sequences and increases padding waste. Cache provided minimal win because prompts are unique per sample.
- Slot-filling family: cache fragmentation surfaced; prefix-only cache hit rate dropped to 12% with high prompt diversity, but KV cache for repeated suffixes retained 30% effectiveness.
- Quantized 4-bit variant: strong cost wins (roughly 30% lower cost per token) but p99 tail degraded in multi-tenant node by ~12% under contention (kernel fallback observed). On dedicated node p99 remained acceptable.

Representative numbers (short-turn, decoder model, dedicated node):
- baseline (batch1, cache off, max_tokens 128): p50 90ms, p95 210ms, p99 420ms, tokens/sec 2200, est cost per 10k requests $3.8
- tuned (batch32, prefix+kv, max_tokens 64): p50 85ms, p95 260ms, p99 500ms, tokens/sec 8700, est cost per 10k requests $0.9
Notes: p95/p99 got worse in tuned case because of queuing under microburst; median unaffected.

Operational observations and anomalies:
- Queueing vs batching tradeoff: when microburst 95th percentile inter-arrival time < batching-window, request latency climbs steeply. We measured a 'batched-wait' component that accounts for up to 60ms at batch_target 32 (configurable in runtime).
- Cache rebuilding cost: first requests after a cache miss sequence incur a KV-load penalty (30-50ms) which can create visible jitter on p95 for interactive workloads. Not a problem for high-reuse slot-filling but hurts diverse summarization.
- Eviction ripple: when KV cache size is set aggressively low to save memory, eviction churn caused CPU spikes on the management thread; observed correlated small GC spikes in host metrics.
- Quantization fallback path: certain attention kernels on older drivers fall back to a slower path with quantized tensors — this only happened on the multi-tenant G4 node. Need to gate quantized defaults by node capability.

Quick recommendations (working):
- Default preset for new decoder-like models (if short-turn oriented): batch_target=16 (not 32), cache_mode=prefix+kv, max_tokens=64, burst_sla_policy: if p95 > 300ms in initial smoke tests enable 'cut-batch-on-microburst' (runtime knob to force small batches when arrival rate spikes).
- For long-context models (summarization): batch_target=8, cache_mode=off, max_tokens=512, prefer fp16 until quantized kernels validated on target hardware.
- Quantized models: only enable auto-quantized default for dedicated/dedicated-like nodes; add a preflight kernel compatibility check (see GH#repo/inference-experiments/pr/142).

Open questions and next experiments:
- Can we make batching adaptive per-route with arrival-rate smoothing to avoid p95 spikes during microbursts? Prototype idea: maintain EWMA arrival rate and cap batch-wait delay subject to predicted tail impact.
- Is there a cheap cache admission policy to avoid fragmentation (e.g., only cache prefixes seen > N times in 24h)? Need to test with production traces.
- Evaluate cost+quality with mixed-quantization (only k/v cache quantized) to see if tail behavior improves.
- Need a small AB test with a customer-facing route to validate median vs tail trade-offs in real traffic.

Action items / next steps:
- (Maya) Add a runtime flag to experiment branch to disable large-batch waiting window and run 48h microburst replay (JIRA-ML-2981).
- (Ravi) Run a dedicated node kernel-compat matrix for quantized kernels and assemble a safe-gate list (due 2026-05-18).
- (Lena) Prepare a short one-pager for product with recommended defaults and fallback policies (target 2026-05-20).
- (Owen) Hook up cost-estimator script to nightly infra to capture GPU-time amortization per model variant. Link: GH#repo/cost-tools/issue/77.

Appendix (notes, shorthand):
- "batched-wait" = configured max delay before dispatching smaller-than-target batch; measured separately in traces.
- "cache_mode" shorthand: prefix-only (store initial token logits for repeated beginnings), prefix+kv (also store KV cache for autoregressive runs).
- Data used: internal promptset v2.1 (600 samples), APIGW synthetic microburst derived from trace 2026-04-22.

Rough confidence: medium. This is a scan to prioritize where we invest deeper gridsearch resources. For final onboarding checklist we need longer runs, per-route traces, and a QA run with customer promptset.

End of notebook.
